findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical state-propagation dynamic program. It maps each stone to the reachable last-jump lengths, starts from jump zero to enforce the first unit jump, deduplicates equivalent states, and uses precise algorithmic names. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 403 and its Python canCross surface. The Reference preserves forward stone-only landings, the exact first jump, all three subsequent jump choices, both source examples with complete explanations, strict position ordering, and all four constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064716842. Its reachable-state map, initialization, ordered propagation, three successor lengths, stone lookup, state insertion, and final reachability test are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the LeetCode wrapper and annotation.

The legal 16-, 32-, and 64-stone tiers span 4x and combine dense reachable prefixes with unreachable final gaps, forcing broad state propagation. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.00 relative growth and 1.00x; a correct predecessor-edge dynamic program that scans every earlier edge passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.30 and 32.07x.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the exact jump rules, both source examples in order with full path and gap explanations, the forward-only requirement, and all four constraints.
